Minimum qualifications:
PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Cognitive Science, Computational Social Science, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), or a related quantitative STEM discipline, or equivalent practical research experience.
One or more first-author peer-reviewed scientific publications at academic venues (e.g., CHI, UIST, CSCW, NeurIPS, ICML) or public preprint repositories.
Experience modeling and predicting human behavior when using interactive systems.
Experience with core research methodologies, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and User Interface (UI) design.
Experience with one or more of the following: computational cognitive modeling, simulated user co-pilots, human-agent collaboration, or Generative AI.

Preferred qualifications:
1 year of experience initiating, scoping, and executing independent research agendas or leading collaborative scientific projects in human-AI systems.
Experience contributing to highly cited seminal papers, widely adopted open-source research frameworks, or recognized international scientific awards and fellowships.
Experience in PAIR's core strategic focus areas: interactive code or music synthesis, LLM steerability, developer tools, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and simulated human behavior alignment.
Experience with interdisciplinary research bridging cognitive science, computer science, machine learning, and human-computer interaction (HCI).
Experience building novel user interfaces, visualization tools, or sandbox environments to inspect, simulate, and evaluate human-agent interactions.
About the job

The People and AI Research (PAIR) team conducts foundational research to make human-AI partnerships productive, enjoyable, and fair. Based in Cambridge, MA, our multidisciplinary team of computer scientists, research engineers, social scientists, and designers invents novel interaction paradigms and develops open-source tools that shape how people interact with intelligent systems.

As a Research Scientist in Human-AI Interaction and Simulation, you will develop computational, cognitive, and statistical models of human behavior to understand, predict, and optimize how people interact with advanced AI systems. Generative models, multimodal assistants, and autonomous agents are transforming interactive computing. Designing effective human-AI partnerships requires models of human cognitive limits, trust dynamics, steerability, and collaboration patterns.

In this role, you will design empirical user studies, build predictive simulations of user interaction, and translate behavioral insights into architectural and UX improvements across Google DeepMind's frontier models.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
Responsibilities
Develop, validate, and land models of human behavior in the context of human-AI interactions, translating complex behavioral insights into actionable improvements for frontier AI models, interactive tools, and user interfaces.
Focus on model integration and applied product impact across Google DeepMind's systems, pivoting focus from academic publishing to direct, applied contributions to frontier models.
Conduct empirical experiments, build interactive research prototypes, and run simulations to evaluate human-agent collaboration, validate hypotheses, and refine research methodologies.
Define data structures, simulation frameworks, experimental designs, and evaluation metrics for research solution development, establishing clear execution timelines and resource needs.
Identify emerging research areas through internal and external collaborations, helping develop long-term strategies to expand Google DeepMind’s applied scientific impact.
